ownership_reason: Only the gold multiplies the factors and holds the product's binary exponent: hop 1 copies the diagonal of the Cholesky factor L^T into an array, and hops 2-4 pass the array along and return the gold's value unchanged. The gold's javadoc promises the product of the squares of the entries; the variant returns that product times 2 to the sum of its running exponents (2^47 on the trigger matrix), a factor that depends on every running product inside the gold, so no caller can pre-filter the entries or recover the product without recomputing it. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact siblings LUDecompositionImpl.getDeterminant and EigenDecompositionImpl.getDeterminant give a determinant as the plain product of a factor's diagonal or of the eigenvalues, with no extra factor, and MathUtils.scalb (d x 2^scaleFactor) fixes that scaling by -e and later by the accumulated exponent cancel; LUSolverTest::testDeterminant, MathUtilsTest::testScalb and CholeskyDecompositionImplTest::testMatricesValues (the factor's diagonal 1, 3, 6, 10, 15) pass.
